Bug #1 (Interval.fromISO + Settings.throwOnInvalid): investigating now — I've located the cause in src/interval.js and am applying the fix plus running the full test suite. ETA ~10 min.

`match` (src/impl/tokenParser.js:247) returns the two-element array `[null, {}]`: `String.prototype.match` gives `null` for a non-matching input, and the function returns that as the first element together with an empty matches object as the second element (the `else` branch at line 264-266). So callers get `rawMatches === null` and `matches === {}` (an empty object, not null).

Bug #4 (DateTime#plus across the 100 barrier through February): I've traced it to `objToLocalTS` in src/impl/util.js — the year-fixup for years 0–99 re-uses the already-normalized 19XX date instead of re-setting month/day, which shifts dates by a day when the arithmetic crosses into a leap year (2000) and lands in year 100 (not a leap year). Fixing and verifying now. ETA ~12 min.

(Note `weeksInWeekYear(obj.weekYear)` is still evaluated for `validWeek`, but it just yields NaN and doesn't throw.)

When the argument is falsy (e.g. `""`), the setter takes the `if (!z)` branch and sets the internal `defaultZone` variable to `null` (src/settings.js:49-55). It does not call `normalizeZone`, so `Settings.defaultZone` then falls back to `LocalZone.instance` (the system's local zone).

Bug #4: fix applied to objToLocalTS in src/impl/util.js (the year 0-99 fix-up now re-applies year/month/day instead of only shifting the year, which was folding a phantom Feb 29); verification run is in flight — ETA ~2 min.

Bug #11 fixed and verified. In src/duration.js the `casualMatrix.quarters` object was missing its `seconds` entry (the `accurateMatrix.quarters` counterpart has one), so quarter<->second conversions produced NaN. Added `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60`. Verified: all 14 duration suites / 114 tests pass, and a temporary check that normalizes all 72 ordered unit pairs (plus exact quarter/second round-trips) passes. No pre-existing test regressed.

Bug #15 (toISODate negative-year padding): found it — `padStart` in src/impl/util.js pads the whole string including the minus sign, so a small negative year like -5 comes out as "00-5" instead of "-0005" (it only looks right for long years like -118040 because the string is already longer than the pad width). Fixing `padStart` to keep the sign outside the padding, then verifying. ETA ~6 min.

It's abstract: `get type()` in src/zone.js:13 just `throw new ZoneIsAbstractError()`. The `Zone` class is an interface (marked `@interface`, with `/* eslint no-unused-vars: "off" */`), so `type` — like `name`, `universal`, `offsetName`, `formatOffset`, `offset`, `equals` and `isValid` — has no implementation and every concrete zone subclass is expected to override it (e.g. `"local"`, `"iana"`, `"fixed"`).

It returns a `FixedOffsetZone` built from that value: `zone = new FixedOffsetZone(matches.Z)` (src/impl/tokenParser.js:303-304), and `dateTimeFromMatches` returns `[vals, zone]`. (`matches.Z` is the offset in minutes produced by the `Z`/`ZZ`/`ZZZ` token handlers, so e.g. parsing `+06:00` yields `FixedOffsetZone.instance(360)`.) That branch takes precedence over `matches.z` (which would give `IANAZone.create(matches.z)`); if neither is defined, `zone` is `null`.

Bug #8 fixed and verified. In src/datetime.js the `isInDST` getter sampled `this.set({ month: 1 })` / `this.set({ month: 5 })`, which keep the day-of-month; in 1974 (US DST Jan 6 – Oct 27) those samples landed inside the DST period, so the comparison was false. The sampled months are now pinned to the 1st (`{ month: 1, day: 1 }`, `{ month: 5, day: 1 }`). Verified: across all 365 days of 1974 at noon in America/New_York the getter is now wrong on 0 days (it was wrong on 320), Jan 6/Jun 1/Oct 26 → true and Jan 5/Oct 27–Dec 31 → false, and all pre-existing isInDST tests (incl. southern-hemisphere Sydney) still pass. No pre-existing test regressed.

Bug #15 fixed and verified. In src/impl/util.js `padStart` padded the whole string including the minus sign, so `padStart(-5, 4)` gave "00-5"; `DateTime.fromObject({ year: -5, month: 5, day: 25, zone: "utc" }).toISODate()` returned "00-5-05-25" instead of "-0005-05-25". The sign is now kept outside the padding. Verified: -5 → "-0005-05-25", -1 → "-0001-01-01", -99 → "-0099-12-31", while +118040/-118040, 1982-05-25, times, RFC 2822 and SQL output are unchanged; the only failing tests in the suite are the 2 pre-existing ICU French toFormat ones. No pre-existing test regressed.

Hour 24 is valid only when the whole time is exactly midnight at the end of the day: `hour === 24 && minute === 0 && second === 0 && millisecond === 0` (src/impl/conversions.js:141-143). Otherwise `validHour` is `integerBetween(hour, 0, 23)`, so 24 with any nonzero minute/second/millisecond is rejected as "unit out of range".

Bug #1 fixed. src/interval.js `Interval.fromISO` now wraps each `DateTime.fromISO` call in try/catch (treating a throw as "not a valid DateTime"), so duration-sided ISO intervals such as "2007-03-01T13:00:00/P1Y2M10DT2H30M" parse instead of throwing when Settings.throwOnInvalid is true; the unparsable message typo ("asISO") was corrected too. Interval tests pass; final full-suite re-check running.
Bug #4 fixed and verified (objToLocalTS in src/impl/util.js now re-applies year/month/day for years 0-99 instead of only shifting the year, so 0099-12-31 + 61 days = 0100-03-02).
Bug #8 fixed and verified (isInDST in src/datetime.js now samples Jan 1 / May 1, so 1974's Jan 6 - Oct 27 DST period is detected; 0 wrong days across 1974).
Bug #11 fixed and verified (missing `seconds` entry added to casualMatrix.quarters in src/duration.js; all 72 unit pairs now normalize without NaN).
Bug #15 fixed and verified (padStart in src/impl/util.js keeps the minus sign outside the padding, so year -5 renders as "-0005-05-25").

Bug #18: fix applied to src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js (`isValid` now returns `isNumber(this.fixed)` instead of hard-coded `true`, so a FixedOffsetZone built with a non-numeric offset is invalid and DateTimes using it are invalid); verification run in flight — ETA ~3 min.

'narrow', 'short', and 'techie' (src/zone.js:48-58): the docstring says it "Accepts 'narrow', 'short', or 'techie'. Returning '+6', '+06:00', or '+0600' respectively". Any other value is out of range — `formatOffset` in src/impl/util.js throws a RangeError for unknown formats.

Bug #18 fixed and verified. In src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js the `isValid` getter was hard-coded to `true`; it now returns `isNumber(this.fixed)` (with `isNumber` imported from ../impl/util.js). So `new FixedOffsetZone("blorp")` / `new FixedOffsetZone(undefined)` are invalid, and a DateTime in such a zone (`DateTime.local().setZone(new FixedOffsetZone("blorp"))`, `DateTime.fromObject({ zone: new FixedOffsetZone("blorp") })`) is itself invalid, while utcInstance / instance(60) / parseSpecifier("UTC+6") stay valid. All zones+info tests pass and the full suite shows only the 2 pre-existing ICU French toFormat failures.

It returns `LocalZone.instance` — the getter is `return defaultZone || LocalZone.instance;` (src/settings.js:61-63). So when the module-level `defaultZone` variable is `null` (its initial value, or after `Settings.defaultZoneName = ""`), `Settings.defaultZone` falls back to the system's local zone rather than returning null.
